notes: **Orbit vs orbital (10-point delta):** (1) an orbit is a definite circular path; an orbital is a region of high probability. (2) Orbits are planar; orbitals are three-dimensional. (3) Orbits come from Bohr's model; orbitals from quantum mechanics. (4) An orbit has a fixed radius; an orbital has no sharp boundary. (5) Orbits are described by one quantum number (n); orbitals by three (n, l, m). (6) Orbits imply exact position and momentum; orbitals obey the uncertainty principle. (7) Orbits can hold at most 2nÂ² electrons; orbitals hold at most 2 electrons. (8) Orbits are circular; orbitals have varied shapes (spherical, dumb-bell, etc.). (9) Orbits are not observable; orbitals are mapped by probability density ÏˆÂ². (10) Orbits were abandoned; orbitals are the accepted modern description.
